wv_bozoo_bouldering.blurb: Bozoo Bouldering sits on a ridge above the New River at Shanklin's Ferry in southern West Virginia. Boulders and mini-cliffs are strung along a crumbling cliff band for roughly two and a half miles. The rock is fine-grained, very hard sandstone often compared with New River Gorge stone; it dries quickly even in cold, snowy weather, and most of the climbing faces south, so winter is a good time to visit. It is entirely bouldering, with a broad spread of problems and a strong concentration of moderates from V2 to V6, plus a handful above V8. The rock is featured but not holdy, so problem-solving matters. Main Area, Downstream Boulderfield, Bozooka Area and Entryway Boulders hold most of it.

wi_interstate_park.blurb: Interstate Park is on the Wisconsin bank of the St. Croix River at St. Croix Falls, facing its Minnesota twin across the gorge. The rock is very old basalt, highly textured in places and smooth and almost sandstone-like in others, with almost none of the water-polished stone found on the Minnesota side. Bouldering accounts for most of the climbs, with problems from V0 to about V8, mostly easy to middle grades. Trad and top-rope lines add moderate climbing, mostly 5.8 to 5.10 with a few harder. The climbing is generally set apart from the busy hiking trails. Biggest areas are Potholes Trail, Cave Boulders, Wisconsin Strip and Sentinel Area.

az_arizona_strip_the.blurb: The Arizona Strip is the arid northwest corner of Arizona, cut off from the rest of the state by the Grand Canyon, and its climbing lies near Mesquite, Nevada. It is nearly all limestone sport climbing, mostly 5.10 to 5.13, with a few easier routes and a couple of 5.14s. Lime Kiln Canyon is the largest area: the Grail has long single pitches on vertical to slightly overhanging rock and stays mostly shady, while the Sacred Trust gets more sun and suits colder days. The Back Walls and Redbud Canyon offer slabbier, grey limestone with more moderate grades. Virgin River Gorge, near I-15, has tall walls of clean stone. Fall and spring are best; winter is cold and summer hot.

nj_b_north_central.blurb: North Central covers Passaic and Morris counties in northern New Jersey. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, spread across parks and ridges rather than gathered in one spot, on erratics, outcroppings and short cliff bands. Problems include faces, slabs, cracks, overhangs and highballs, mostly V0 to V5 with a scattering of harder lines up to about V11. The Ramapo ridges hold granite and gneiss, while the Green Pond Mountain ridges have purple-tinted quartzite conglomerate. A handful of top-rope lines exist, though their quality is limited, along with a few ice routes. Pyramid Mountain, with its Ball Field Boulders, is one of the main concentrations.

az_west_sedona.blurb: West Sedona covers the western side of town, spread across the Dry Creek basin and the deep canyons that drop off the Mogollon Rim, at roughly 4,500 feet. Trad dominates, with a smaller share of sport, a few top-rope lines and a couple of aid routes, and multi-pitch climbs are common. Grades center on 5.9 to 5.11, with a decent number of 5.7 and 5.8 routes below and a few 5.12s and 5.13s above. The Dry Creek Road Area is by far the largest, followed by the Chimney Rock Area and the Coffeepot Rock Area. Chimney Rock itself is a pair of fin-like towers with a few established lines, mostly toward the harder end of the spectrum.

nm_roy.blurb: Roy is a remote bouldering area in northeastern New Mexico, in ranch country along the Canadian River valley, where the river has cut canyons through Dakota sandstone. The stone is very hard, with textured slopers, crisp edges and many tall highballs, in a wide-open, wild setting. Most climbs are boulder problems, from V0 up past V10, with the bulk in the V1 to V8 range. Some sport and trad routes add roped climbing, mainly from 5.10 to 5.12. Middle Mesteno, Mills Canyon, Upper Mesteno and the Overlook are the main sectors. The best season runs from mid-fall to mid-spring, with winter prime for cool air and good friction; summer is generally too hot.
